newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine Merval closes up 0.56 pct in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Merval closes up 0.56 pct in slow trade.

text.p: The Buenos Aires Stock Exchange recovered Thursday early-session losses to close slightly up in low-volume trade.

"The market was feeling apathetic today," said broker Miguel Daneri from Boston Securities. "There was bad feeling over the fact that Congress did not sit, and there was only a sporadic supply of ADRs at certain prices."
The blue-chip Merval .MERV index closed up 0.56 percent at 537.63. Turnover totaled $15.5 million, up from Wednesday's miserly 10.3 million.
"There's not much trading spirit around. There was very low volume,"said Cristina Hintz of Provincia Bursatil.

She said the market was unnerved by the government's continuing failure to make Congress pass a package of key measures to raise taxes and reduce the budget deficit, and at continual modifications being made to the measures.

Hintz said traders were also saddened by the blackout protest being planned for Thursday night by opposition groups. The opposition Radical and Frepaso parties have called on Argentines to turn their lights off for five minutes in protest at the government's economic policies.
But cheer for brokers came from bonds, which were performing with more gusto than shares.
"Everything's going well with bonds. There's a lot of money coming to Latin America. It improves the (country) risk situation," said Hintz.

"The bond market is growing fast and is lending strength to shares," said Dineri. "Bonds are getting their strength from the lower yields in U.S. long bonds, and from the possibility that Brazil might buy back old debt to take out new debt."
"Argentina could be next on the list of countries that opt for this type of operation," said Daneri.
The broad-market index rose 0.59 percent to 16,551.5, with 20 rises, 21 falls and 19 stocks unchanged. Turnover rose to $117 million from $72.4 million Wednesday.

The strongest risers were oil company Astra, up 3.2 percent, petrochemical company Ipako, up 1.9 percent, and oil firm YPF, up 1.6 percent. Biggest losers were Banco de Galicia, down 2.3 percent, carmaker Ciadea, down 2.2 percent, and Banco Frances, slipping 1.9 percent.
